name: Dentifrices (toothpaste, gel, powder, tablets)
anchor: sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant schedules with the Germany BVL 2017 TOOTHPASTE tier as the oral-mucosal anchor for formulated products, and Canada SOR/2018-83's mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling as the article anchor
native_basis: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total content, ug/kg as sold)
native_basis_label: finished oral-care product as placed on market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of product as sold (ug/kg). Not a dietary maximum level and not a migration/leachate value.
scope_note: Toothpastes, tooth gels, tooth powders and chewable or dissolving toothpaste tablets for adults and the general population, including fluoride dentifrices marketed under an OTC drug monograph: the taxonomy's first boundary rule routes by exposure pathway (oral cavity) and not by regulatory classification, so a monograph anticaries claim does not move the product out of this row. Children's dentifrices for ages 0-5 route to Category 2 (Infant and Child Personal Care) and that row must be at least as strict as this one. Dedicated whitening systems (peroxide strips, gels, trays, pens) route to the whitening-products row; a whitening CLAIM on a conventional dentifrice keeps the product here. This is the only row in the category that a sovereign toothpaste-specific instrument directly regulates.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(colourant|colorant|colour additive|color additive|migration|leachate|food-contact|accessible part|candy as sold|as consumed|wet weight|toy))(?=.*(cosmetic|finished toothpaste|finished oral))
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor on a formulated oral row must be a FINISHED-COSMETIC (or finished oral-product) total-content instrument, and the guard's positive test admits only a basis that says so: 'cosmetic', 'finished toothpaste' or 'finished oral'. It rejects three families that would otherwise conflate bases: colour-additive and ingredient purity specifications (21 CFR 73/74, the India permitted-colours entry), which cap one raw material and not the finished product; migration and leachate values (EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy migration, food-contact migration), which measure release rather than content; and DIETARY maximum levels, which are now excluded structurally rather than by keyword, because a food-commodity maximum level cannot satisfy a positive test for a cosmetic basis. This guard was corrected on 2026-08-17. Its earlier form also admitted any register row whose basis read 'product as sold'. Measured against the register on 2026-08-17, that admitted 176 rows to a guard whose published purpose was to exclude dietary values, 99 of them carrying no cosmetic basis at all: 84 Singapore Food Regulations maximum levels, the Mexican NOM-186 cocoa-butter lead value (100 ug/kg, STRICTER than this row's published lead value and therefore capable of binding it), the GSO concentrated-juice value and the Japanese pet-food values. No shipped number was ever in the wrong basis, because no dietary id was named and the audit scope would not surface one, but the sole mechanical firewall against the conflation Method v2.0 forbids was inoperative and its published description was refutable from the register the document cites as its own source. The property verified after the correction is stated as an invariant rather than as a row count, because the register is appended to continuously and any fixed count would go stale: EVERY row that passes this guard carries 'cosmetic' in its basis, and NO row whose product scope is a food, feed or fertiliser commodity passes. Both halves are re-checkable against the register at any time by applying this guard string to each row's basis and basis_class, which is exactly how the compiler applies it. A basis failure resolves the cell to a GAP and fails the build rather than publishing a number in the wrong basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total lead content, ug/kg as sold)
Pb.label: Germany BVL 2017 publishes a toothpaste-specific technically-avoidable lead content of 0.5 mg/kg, four times stricter than its own general-cosmetic tier (2 mg/kg), because a dentifrice sits on the oral mucosa and is partly swallowed. It is the strictest applicable sovereign value for this exact cell. The only other toothpaste-specific instrument, Washington State's Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act at 1 mg/kg, is twice as loose and cannot bind; it is disclosed in the substantiation below and remains inside this row's audit scan, but it is not carried in the candidate set because its register basis string is not specific enough to pass this row's corrected basis guard.
Pb.substantiation: Germany BVL 2017 is the only instrument in the register that publishes a SEPARATE, STRICTER toothpaste tier alongside its general-cosmetic tier. That tier exists because a dentifrice is applied to the oral mucosa and is partly swallowed, which is the exposure pattern every formulated row in this category shares. The binding German value carries register status 'guidance impurity limit' (the BVL technically-avoidable-content table, the basis on which German competent authorities object to a cosmetic under Regulation (EC) 1223/2009 Article 17); the selection is not a status judgement and does not depend on one. WASHINGTON STATE IS DISCLOSED AND NOT NAMED. Its Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act toothpaste lead value (register id wa_tfca_pb_toothpaste_1000) is a statutory limit at 1000 ug/kg, twice as loose as the German value, so it could never bind this cell. It is not carried in the candidate set because its register basis reads only 'product as sold' — a string that identifies neither the cosmetic nor the oral form, and that consequently cannot pass this row's corrected basis guard, which admits only a basis naming a cosmetic or finished oral product. Correcting that register basis is logged as a register gap for the verified regulatory-fetch pathway rather than done here, because the same register row is named by the children's-toothpaste row of the Category 2 standard under a looser guard, and amending the basis in isolation would resolve that sibling cell to a GAP. Washington remains inside this row's audit scan: jurisdiction US-WA is in the credible set and its product scope 'toothpaste' matches the audit scope, so were the value ever revised below the German tier the compiler would flag it as a stricter unselected anchor rather than let it pass unnoticed.

Cd.basis: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total cadmium content, ug/kg as sold)
Cd.label: The BVL toothpaste cadmium tier (0.1 mg/kg) binds. It is identical to the BVL general-cosmetic cadmium value, so for cadmium the oral tier adds no additional stringency; it is thirty times stricter than the next-strictest surveyed sovereign value (Health Canada and Thailand, 3 mg/kg).
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium reaches dentifrices through mineral abrasives, phosphate raw materials and colour pigments. Eleven sovereign finished-cosmetic instruments were surveyed and are named in the candidate set; the German value binds by a factor of thirty.

tAs.basis: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total arsenic content, ug/kg as sold)
tAs.label: The BVL toothpaste total-arsenic tier (0.5 mg/kg) binds, identical to the BVL general-cosmetic value and four times stricter than the next-strictest surveyed sovereign value (Kenya KS 2937 and China NMPA 2015, 2 mg/kg).
tAs.substantiation: This is a TOTAL-arsenic value. It does not satisfy the inorganic-arsenic cell and is not satisfied by an inorganic-arsenic determination; inorganic arsenic is separately controlled by reflex speciation on the iAs cell and is bounded by this value by identity.

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic. No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for any oral-care product: every sovereign arsenic value in the cosmetic instrument family (Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, Korea MFDS, Taiwan MOHW, ASEAN and its national transpositions, Kenya KS 2937, EAEU TR CU 009/2011) is a TOTAL-arsenic value, and every sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level in the register is a food, feed or fertiliser commodity value on a dietary or dry-matter basis (rice and rice products, fish and other marine products, fruit juice, milk and dairy, meat and offal, sugar, edible salt, edible oils and fats, gelatine and collagen, pet food, and the EU fertilising-product classes), and not one is scoped to a cosmetic, an oral-care product or a consumer article. The cell is therefore held under reflex speciation rather than given an invented ceiling; inorganic arsenic cannot exceed total arsenic by identity, so the published total-arsenic value (500 ug/kg) is its upper bound.
iAs.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation on any lot whose total-arsenic screen exceeds 50% of the published total-arsenic value. The inorganic fraction is held under ALARA against the tightest available context and any unexplained inorganic arsenic triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay, mineral-pigment or botanical-extract input that carries it.

tHg.basis: finished dentifrice as placed on market (total mercury content, ug/kg as sold)
tHg.label: The BVL toothpaste total-mercury tier (0.1 mg/kg) binds, identical to the BVL general-cosmetic value and ten times stricter than the near-universal 1 mg/kg cosmetic mercury allowance (US FDA 21 CFR 700.13, Health Canada, China, Korea, Taiwan, ASEAN and its transpositions, India, EAEU).
tHg.substantiation: This is a TOTAL-mercury value and it bounds the methylmercury cell by identity. The US instrument named in the candidate set, 21 CFR 700.13, is a binding adulteration rule rather than a guidance figure; it is ten times looser than the German value and does not bind.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and bioaccumulates in fish muscle. A dentifrice, rinse, whitening or denture-care matrix has no methylating microbial community and no marine input; the mercury sources that reach this category are mineral-abrasive, clay and pigment impurities, which are inorganic. Methylmercury is a species of total mercury and cannot exceed it (MeHg <= tHg), so any mercury present is governed by and bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling of 100 ug/kg on this row.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold or CV-AAS. No separate methylmercury determination is required for an oral-care matrix; any lot above 50% of the total-mercury ceiling is investigated to its mercury source before release.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Every sovereign methylmercury maximum level in the register is scoped to fish and seafood. The applicable oral-care mercury instrument (Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier, 100 ug/kg) is a TOTAL-mercury value, and it bounds methylmercury by identity.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: Germany BVL 2017 (toothpaste and general-cosmetic tiers); US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Washington State Toxics-Free Cosmetics Act; Health Canada Guidance on Heavy Metal Impurities in Cosmetics; China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards; Korea MFDS Notice 2024-9 and Notice 2025-63; Taiwan MOHW 2024; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 and the Indonesian (BPOM 16/2024), Malaysian (NPRA 2022), Singaporean (HSA 2024) and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011 — none sets a methylmercury value.

Ni.basis: finished oral-care product as placed on market (total nickel content, ug/kg as sold) — read across from the Korean residual finished-cosmetic nickel tier
Ni.source_scope: cosmetic products other than eye makeup or color makeup products
Ni.label: No sovereign names nickel in an oral-care product. Korea MFDS is the only jurisdiction in the register that sets a finished-cosmetic nickel content limit at all, and it tiers it by product type: eye makeup 35 ug/g, colour makeup 30 ug/g, and all other cosmetic products 10 ug/g. An oral-care product is neither eye makeup nor a colour cosmetic, so the residual 'other products' tier — the STRICTEST of the three — is the nearest applicable sovereign cell and is read across. The named anchor is MFDS Notice No. 2025-63 (Cosmetics Safety Standards), the current Korean instrument. HMTc does not use the looser makeup tiers.
Ni.substantiation: Nickel is a mucosal and contact sensitiser and reaches oral-care formulations through hydrated-silica and calcium-carbonate abrasives, mineral pigments, and stainless-steel process contact, so the cell must not be left without a ceiling where a sovereign anchor exists. The exact cell (nickel in a dentifrice, rinse, whitening system or denture-care product) is unregulated in every jurisdiction surveyed, which is why the value is published as a disclosed read-across tagged 'read-across' rather than as regulatory alignment; in Korea a dentifrice is a quasi-drug rather than a cosmetic, so the Korean cosmetic tier does not reach this form by its own terms. Two Korean notices state the same three-tier allowance at identical values: Notice 2024-9 Article 6(2) (kr_mfds2024_9_ni_other_cosmetics_10ugg) and the current Notice No. 2025-63 (the named anchor). The later notice is cited so that this standard and the Category 2 children's-dentifrice standard, which anchors the same cell, cite the same current instrument rather than splitting across two Korean notices for one number. The value is 10000 ug/kg under either notice, neither register row is flagged superseded, and the 2024-9 row remains inside this row's audit scan.

Sn.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a tin content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the sovereign tin maximum levels in the register are canned-food and food-contact values written for tinplate migration into food and are a different basis entirely. Tin is additionally not a pure impurity in this category: stannous fluoride and stannous chloride are authorised anticaries and antigingivitis actives in dentifrices and mouthrinses, so a finished-product tin ceiling would be exceeded by design in a compliant stannous formulation and would be meaningless as a contaminant control. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because tin is unambiguously present at material levels in this category and an absence claim would be contradicted on its face.
Sn.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-tin analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, reconciled against the batch record's declared stannous input. Tin in excess of the stoichiometric contribution of the declared stannous active, or any quantifiable tin in a product with no declared tin-bearing ingredient, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context). No numeric ceiling is published.

Al.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Aluminium is also frequently an intentional, declared functional ingredient in this category rather than a contaminant: hydrated alumina and aluminium oxide are conventional dentifrice abrasives, aluminium hydroxide is a common excipient, and aluminium lakes are the substrate of most permitted cosmetic colours. A finished-product aluminium ceiling would therefore be exceeded by design in a compliant alumina-abrasive formulation. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control with a declaration reconciliation rather than declared not-material, because aluminium is unambiguously present at material levels in this category.
Al.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-aluminium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold (ICP-OES permitted where a high-alumina abrasive system saturates the ICP-MS working range), reconciled against the batch record's declared aluminium-bearing ingredients. Aluminium beyond the declared ingredient contribution triggers supplier corrective action on the abrasive, clay or pigment input under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule. No numeric ceiling is published.

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product; the chromium values reachable from this category are all written on other bases and are excluded by this row's basis guard — the EU toy figures (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3), the China GB 21027 student-article values, the Mexico NOM-252 toy and school-article values and ASTM F963 are migration, soluble or bioavailable-fraction determinations, and the EU plastic food-contact value is a specific-migration limit into food. Total chromium is in any case a screen rather than a protective ceiling, since it is dominated by benign Cr(III) while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI). The cell is held under mandatory analytical control feeding the Cr(VI) reflex below, and no number is invented.
Cr.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-chromium analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold. Total chromium is used as the screen that triggers the Cr(VI) reflex; any result above the analytical reporting limit that cannot be traced to a declared Cr(III) pigment or to stainless-steel process contact is escalated to supplier corrective action.

Cr-VI.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit for any oral-care or cosmetic product. Cr(VI) is deliberately NOT registered as a method-artifact not-material determination in this category: the method-artifact basis rests on Cr(VI) reducing to Cr(III) in the matrix, and oral-care matrices routinely contain oxidising systems — hydrogen peroxide and carbamide peroxide whiteners, sodium percarbonate and persulfate denture cleansers, peroxide-containing rinses — in which that reduction cannot be assumed. The cell is a control with a reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on any elevated total-chromium screen: alkaline extraction per EPA 3060A with IC-ICP-MS determination per EPA 6800, or EN 15192 for solid and paste matrices. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails the lot and blocks release pending supplier corrective action.
